selectedStory.title: The Fall of NVIDIA's King: How Jensen Huang Lost the Company He Built
selectedStory.editorialAngle: A corporate governance and national-security crisis around the resignation of NVIDIA co-founder Jensen Huang, the board's refusal to reinstate him, and the challenge of leading the AI infrastructure giant without its iconic founder.
selectedStory.framing: Huang resigned; the board accepted the resignation and later said it did not intend to reinstate him. Do not label the event a firing as an established fact.

claims.text: NVIDIA disclosed that Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member effective immediately; the board accepted his resignation.
claims.caveat: The SEC filing dates the accepted resignation November 11; the company announcement was published November 12.

claims.text: Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
The board said it initiated an independent investigation after reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
claims.caveat: This records what the board said, not proof that the reported effort occurred or succeeded.

claims.text: On November 17, the board chair said the board did not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO.
claims.caveat: Attribute the statement to board chair Harvey Jones; do not imply a court or regulator made this determination.

claims.text: Huang publicly said he would be honored to return if the board determined it was in shareholders' and the company's best interest.
Huang and NVIDIA's general counsel agreed to appear for transcribed congressional interviews scheduled for December 1 and 2.
claims.caveat: The committee's stated concerns are allegations/questions, not findings of wrongdoing.

claims.text: California's attorney general issued an investigative subpoena to NVIDIA concerning potential chip transfers, disclosures and related matters.
claims.caveat: Based on AP reporting; obtain the subpoena or official DOJ statement before final narration. An investigation is not proof of misconduct.

claims.text: A purported internal employee letter demanding the board resign was fabricated, according to Reuters Fact Check.
claims.caveat: If included, distinguish the fake viral image from the separate genuine open letter supporting a fair hearing for Huang.
